name: Relational model
description: Data is modelled as relations, which are sets of tuples that share the same attributes.

name: Tables, rows and columns
description: A table holds rows, and each row has a value for every column the table defines.

name: Primary key
description: A primary key is a column or set of columns whose values identify each row uniquely.

name: Foreign key
description: A foreign key is a column whose values must match a primary key in another table, linking rows across tables.

name: SELECT basics
description: SELECT reads chosen columns from a table and returns the result as a new set of rows.

name: Filtering with WHERE
description: The WHERE clause keeps only the rows for which a condition is true.

name: Joins
description: A join combines rows from two tables according to a condition, usually a key match.

name: GROUP BY and aggregates
description: GROUP BY collects rows into groups so that functions such as COUNT and SUM can summarise each group.

name: Normalization
description: Normalization splits data across tables so that each fact is stored once, which avoids update anomalies.

name: Denormalization
description: Denormalization deliberately repeats data in a table to make common reads faster at the cost of extra writes.

name: Pages and the buffer pool
description: A database stores data in fixed-size pages on disk and keeps recently used pages in a memory area called the buffer pool.

name: B-trees
description: A B-tree is a balanced, sorted tree of pages that finds a key by visiting a number of nodes proportional to the logarithm of the key count.

name: Indexes
description: An index is an extra structure, most often a B-tree, that lets the database find matching rows without scanning the whole table.

name: Composite indexes
description: A composite index covers several columns in order and can serve filters on its leading columns.

name: Query planning
description: The query planner compares candidate execution plans, estimates their cost, and picks the cheapest one.

name: Transactions
description: A transaction groups several statements so that they succeed or fail together as one unit of work.

name: ACID properties
description: ACID names the four guarantees of a transaction: atomicity, consistency, isolation, and durability.

name: Locking
description: Locking lets a transaction reserve a row or table so that others cannot change it at the same time.

name: Isolation levels
description: Isolation levels define how much of other transactions' uncommitted work one transaction is allowed to see.

name: Multi-version concurrency control
description: Multi-version concurrency control keeps several versions of a row so that readers do not block writers.

name: Deadlocks
description: A deadlock occurs when transactions each wait for a lock that another one holds, so none can continue.

name: Write-ahead log
description: A write-ahead log records each change durably before the data pages are written, so the database can recover after a crash.

name: Replication
description: Replication keeps copies of the same data on several servers, usually by shipping the log from a leader to followers.

name: Partitioning
description: Partitioning splits one large table into smaller parts according to the value of a key.

name: Sharding
description: Sharding spreads partitions of a dataset across several servers so that each server holds only part of the data.
